build: lean-muscled, swimmer's shoulders, strong through the core
hair: black, thick and straight, worn in a long braid down her back or twisted into a crown when she works
complexion: warm golden-brown undertone, a faint scar along her left jawline from a childhood fall on ice
face: a wide, open face with high cheekbones and deep-set dark eyes that telegraph every feeling before her mouth catches up—the kind of face that makes strangers trust her too quickly
signature_feature: her hands—long-fingered, capable, with permanent calluses from printmaking and a habit of moving them when she speaks, as if sculpting the air into sense
second_celebrated_feature: the hollow at the base of her throat, visible when she pulls her hair back, which the LI notices catches light when she breathes
signature_habits: she hums while working—old Inuktitut lullabies her grandmother taught her, half-remembered; she keeps a thermos of strong black tea within arm's reach at all times; she touches her own collarbone when she's anxious, a self-soothing gesture; she speaks with her whole body, rarely still
occupation: independent printmaker and small-press book designer; she runs a studio in a converted warehouse, takes commissions, teaches workshops, and is mid-project on a limited-edition artist's book when the story opens

current_crisis.event: her studio's landlord—a shell company owned by the LI's rival—has served a 30-day eviction notice; she has no capital to relocate, her equipment is bespoke and immobile, and the book project is 60% complete with a gallery opening in eight weeks
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic threaded with a sharp, clarifying rage
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find $80,000 in the next two weeks without losing control of her own work or owing anyone her soul

wound.core: she believes that wanting things—safety, stability, love—is a luxury that will be taken from her, so she has learned to want only what she can make with her own hands
wound.surfacing_hint: when someone offers help, her first instinct is to refuse; when she's cornered, she becomes very still and very quiet, as if bracing for impact
